handbook.about.draft: The handbook is therefore a draft, and the foot of every page says so.
handbook.about.hans: This edition's Simplified text was converted from the Traditional data through the app's own table and has not been reviewed for Mainland usage.
handbook.about.model.scale: Yin and yang and the direction are each drawn on a scale: the middle is even; the further right the mark, the more yang or rising (↑), the further left, the more yin or sinking (↓); a direction inside the grey band in the middle reads as even (either way). The five phases give the herb's share in each phase, in per cent.
handbook.about.model.text: The 'property model' line of an entry gives the coordinates the app derives for the herb, by written rules, from its four natures, five flavours, channel tropism, category, functions and part used; each rule comes with the passage it rests on ({model}). It is a draft: an approximation for study, not a settled account of the herb.
handbook.about.model.title: The property model
handbook.about.read.cautions: the cautions on record, and the herbs the eighteen incompatibilities and the nineteen antagonisms say not to combine it with;
handbook.about.read.facts: its category, nature, flavours, channel tropism, traditional functions and part used, as its source entry gives them;
handbook.about.read.formulas: its formulas: those of the app that use it, and the other classical formulas its source lists;
handbook.about.read.head: its number, its Chinese name, its pinyin (without tone marks), its English name (only the curated herbs have one) and its Latin name;
handbook.about.read.model: the property model's reading: yin and yang, direction, five phases, tonifying or draining, moistening or drying, qi and blood (see {model});
handbook.about.read.relations: where recorded, its seven relations, channel guides and small-or-large use, each with its text;
handbook.about.read.source: its source entry and its review state.
handbook.about.read.title: How to read an entry
handbook.about.review: Review: {derived} herbs are drafts derived from their source entries by rules, {curated} are curated drafts and {reviewed} have been reviewed.
handbook.about.safety.allergy: An allergy to a herb rules that herb out.
handbook.about.safety.incompatible: The whole table of the eighteen incompatibilities and the nineteen antagonisms, with the herbs of this handbook each traditional name covers, is in {safety}; the caution in an entry is the source's own text and may not list them all.
handbook.about.safety.notRecorded: Where no toxicity, pregnancy caution or interaction is shown, none is recorded; that does not make the herb safe, and none of these records has been reviewed by a professional yet.
handbook.about.safety.practitioner: A herb is chosen by a licensed practitioner for the person it is meant for. This handbook only describes the herbs: it gives no doses, and it is not medical advice.
handbook.about.safety.recorded: Each entry starts with the cautions on record: toxicity and its grade, pregnancy and possible interactions, the source's own caution, and the herbs the eighteen incompatibilities and the nineteen antagonisms say not to combine it with.
handbook.about.safety.title: Before use

handbook.bands.intro: The tradition observed that some herbs act differently when used sparingly or in quantity. Each herb below has a passage of its own; the property model switches to the matching reading below or above the usual measure.
handbook.contents.title: Contents
handbook.cover.draft: Draft: the herb records in this handbook were compiled from their source entries by the app's own rules and have not been reviewed by a qualified practitioner or a pharmacist. For study only: not medical advice, and no substitute for an examination by a licensed practitioner. The handbook gives no doses.

handbook.glossary.intro: The terms of the app's glossary in Chinese, pinyin and English; the English follows the World Health Organization's standard terminology for traditional medicine where it has the term, and awaits review.
handbook.lookup.intro: Grouped by nature, flavour and channel tropism, each group in the order of the entries; a herb may stand in several groups.
handbook.mark.none: No toxicity, pregnancy caution or interaction recorded (not yet reviewed by a professional)
handbook.model.direction.value: Direction reading {value} (−1 sinking and descending, +1 rising and floating; within ±{band}, even)
handbook.model.intro: Each reading of the property model is derived by a written rule, and the rule used is recorded: when one is wrong, the rule is changed, not the number. Below are each reading's rules, the passages they rest on, and how the handbook's herbs fall. All of it is a draft awaiting the pharmacy review.
handbook.model.rule.buXie: The category decides first: tonifying herbs read as tonifying, the categories that remove a pathogen or a product as draining. For the other categories the function words decide: only words such as 補, 益, 養, 滋, 填, 生津 and 助陽 make a herb tonifying, only words such as 清, 瀉, 破, 攻, 逐, 化瘀, 消, 利, 祛, 除 and 鎮 draining, and both or neither make it neither. An interior-warming herb is tonifying when it tonifies the fire of the kidney (補火, 補陽, 壯陽, 溫腎), otherwise neither.
handbook.model.rule.buXie.title: Tonifying or draining
handbook.model.rule.direction: The category and the functions count for half: exterior-releasing and emetic herbs rise; purgative, liver-calming, spirit-calming, water-draining, astringent and heat-clearing herbs sink; function words name a direction — 升陽, 舉陷, 發散, 透疹 and 宣肺 up, 降氣, 降逆, 平喘, 潛陽, 重鎮, 瀉下, 利尿 and 引血下行 down. The qi and the flavour count for three tenths: sour and salty never rise, sweet and pungent never sink, cold never floats, heat never sinks. The part used counts for a fifth: flowers and leaves are light and rise, seeds and fruits are heavier, minerals and shells heavy and sink. For the herbs the tradition singles out, its statement applies. Within ±{band} the reading is even (either way).
handbook.model.rule.direction.title: Ascending, descending, floating, sinking
handbook.model.rule.part: As the source entry states the part used; the direction reading draws on it.
handbook.model.rule.part.title: Part used
handbook.model.rule.phases: The phases of the five flavours count for three fifths: sour wood, bitter fire, sweet earth, pungent metal, salty water, with bland counted as sweet and astringent as sour. The five phases of the channel tropism count for two fifths: each channel by the phase of its organ, the first listed weighing most.
handbook.model.rule.phases.title: Five phases
handbook.model.rule.qiXue: Qi-regulating herbs go to the qi aspect, blood-activating and hemostatic herbs to the blood aspect. For the others the function words decide — words such as 補氣, 理氣, 行氣, 降氣 and 疏肝 for qi, 補血, 活血, 化瘀, 止血 and 涼血 for blood; with both, the first-listed function decides, and a first function that names both makes it both (川芎, 活血行氣: a qi herb within the blood). Where neither the functions nor the category say anything, a dry herb goes to the qi aspect and a moist one to the blood aspect.
handbook.model.rule.qiXue.title: Qi and blood
handbook.model.rule.runZao: Function words such as 滋陰, 養陰, 生津, 潤燥, 養血 and 填精 make a herb moistening, words such as 燥濕, 化濕, 祛風濕 and 溫燥 drying; dampness-resolving and wind-damp-dispelling herbs are drying; the curated marks 滋膩 and 燥烈 make it moistening and drying. Where the functions say nothing, a pungent, bitter and warm herb dries and a sweet and cold or cool one moistens; otherwise neither.
handbook.model.rule.runZao.title: Moistening or drying
handbook.model.rule.toxicity: As the source grades it — highly toxic, toxic, slightly toxic, or none recorded: the classical 大毒, 常毒, 小毒 and 無毒. A curated herb may carry a mark set by hand.
handbook.model.rule.toxicity.title: Toxicity
handbook.model.rule.tropism: In the order the source lists the channels, the first weighing most.
handbook.model.rule.tropism.title: Channel tropism
handbook.model.rule.yinyang: The four natures count for half: warm and hot are yang, cool and cold yin. The five flavours count for three tenths: pungent, sweet and bland are yang; sour, bitter and salty yin; astringent counts as sour. The direction counts for a fifth: rising and floating are yang, sinking and descending yin. −1 is wholly yin, +1 wholly yang.
handbook.model.rule.yinyang.title: Yin and yang
handbook.model.yinyang.value: Yin and yang reading {value} (−1 wholly yin, +1 wholly yang)
handbook.names.intro: Latin names as the source gives them, in italics; only the curated herbs have an English name. The number is the entry's.
handbook.pairing.fan.meaning: The two must not be combined. The app never computes it: its safety rules exclude such pairs (see {safety}).
handbook.pairing.sha.meaning: One herb restrains the other's harm: mutual restraint seen from the herb that restrains.
handbook.pairing.shi.meaning: The other herb serves this one and strengthens its action (the text says 「為之使」 or 「得某良」).
handbook.pairing.wei.meaning: This herb fears the other: the other restrains its harm (半夏畏生薑); seen from the other herb, this is mutual suppression (相殺).
handbook.pairing.wu.meaning: This herb dislikes the other: the other takes away from its effect (人參惡萊菔子).
handbook.pairing.xu.meaning: Two herbs of like action, used together, strengthen each other. The pairs in the table are textbook examples, not yet checked.
handbook.pairings.intro: The pairs below were read by the app from the table 「相須相使相畏相惡諸藥」 of 《本草綱目·序例下》 (after 徐之才's 《藥對》), between herbs of this handbook, each with the text it was read from, with the textbook examples of mutual reinforcement besides. All are drafts awaiting the pharmacy review.
handbook.pinyin.intro: In the order of the pinyin, without tone marks; the number is the entry's.
handbook.processing.cleaning: Words for cleaning or cutting, which leave the herb's action as it is: {list}.
handbook.processing.intro: The methods below were read by the app from 《本草蒙筌》: each method's text, the readings of the property model it changes, and how a formula may write it. The one marked as a textbook statement has no classical text. All are drafts awaiting the pharmacy review.
handbook.safety.incompatible: Herbs not to combine: the eighteen incompatibilities and the nineteen antagonisms
handbook.safety.incompatible.intro: The traditional prohibitions on combining herbs, as the app's safety rules hold them. After each traditional name come the herbs of this handbook it covers in that row — 芍藥, for one, covers 白芍 and 赤芍 — and the app matches by these herbs. The table awaits the pharmacy and physician review.
handbook.safety.intro: These lists hold only what the records mark; a herb that is not listed is not thereby safe. None of the records has been reviewed by a professional yet.
handbook.safety.shijiuwei.note: The nineteen antagonisms follow standard textbook teaching, not yet checked against the app's classical texts.
handbook.sources.intro: The works this handbook draws on: the sources of its herb entries, of the relations in its tables and of every passage it quotes. Every passage has been checked against its source.
handbook.strokes.intro: By the stroke count of the name's first character, then in character order; the number is the entry's.

handbook.yinjing.intro: {source} lists, after 潔古's 《珍珠囊》, the herbs that lead a formula to each channel. The table names only the herbs of this handbook; for some channels only some of the herbs the text lists could be matched.
